\subsection{The skew pairing and the double}

Write $\Delta^2(x)=(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(x)
=x_1\otimes x_2\otimes x_3$ (Sweedler notation).  From \eqref{C}:
\begin{align}
\Delta^2(E_r)&=E_r\otimes1\otimes1
  +\cK_r\otimes E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes\cK_r\otimes E_r,
\label{DE}\tag{$\Delta^2$}\\
\Delta^2(F_r)&=F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}\otimes\cK_r^{-1}
  +1\otimes F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}+1\otimes1\otimes F_r .\notag
\end{align}

\begin{definition}\label{def:D}
The \emph{skew pairing}
$\la\cdot,\cdot\ra:\Uq(\bm)\times\Uq(\bp)\to\C$ is the bilinear form
determined by
\begin{align}
\la u,yz\ra&=\la u_1,z\ra\la u_2,y\ra,\qquad
 \la uv,z\ra=\la u,z_1\ra\la v,z_2\ra,\label{PA}\tag{PA}\\
\la1,y\ra&=\vep(y),\qquad\la u,1\ra=\vep(u),\notag\\
&\la\hK_i,\hK_j\ra=q^{a_{ij}},\qquad
\la F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht,\qquad
\la\hK_i,E_r\ra=\la F_s,\hK_j\ra=0 .\label{P}\tag{P}
\end{align}
The \emph{generalized quantum double}
$D=\Uq(\bm)\ptn\Uq(\bp)$ is the associative algebra on the vector
space $\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$ in which $\Uq(\bm)$ and $\Uq(\bp)$
are subalgebras (so $xy=(x\otimes1)(1\otimes y)$ for $x\in\Uq(\bm)$,
$y\in\Uq(\bp)$ internally) with cross multiplication determined by
\begin{equation}
y\,x=\la x_1,y_1\ra\;x_2\,y_2\;\la x_3,S^{-1}y_3\ra
\qquad(x\in\Uq(\bm),\ y\in\Uq(\bp)).\label{SK}\tag{SK}
\end{equation}
computed with the $\Delta^2$-decompositions \eqref{DE} and extended
bilinearly.  This is the Drinfel'd--Tanisaki convention with the
coproducts \eqref{C} unmirrored; every channel computation below is
performed directly in the printed form.
That the form determined by \eqref{PA}--\eqref{P}
descends to the Borel quotients, is nondegenerate, and that
\eqref{SK} then defines an associative algebra with the two Borels as
subalgebras, is the Drinfel'd--Tanisaki skew-pairing construction
(Drinfel'd; Tanisaki, \emph{Killing forms, Harish-Chandra
homomorphisms and universal $\mathcal R$-matrices for quantum
algebras}; Klimyk--Schm\"udgen, \emph{Quantum Groups and their
Representations}, Chap.~8): this existence theorem is the single
external input of the paper.  The consistency of \eqref{PA}--\eqref{P}
with \eqref{H1}--\eqref{H3} is verified elementarily in
Lemma~\ref{lem:compat}, and every constant of the double is computed
below from \eqref{SK} by the channel calculus.
\end{definition}

The recursion \eqref{PA} is evaluated by the \emph{channel calculus}:
group each slot word to grouplike--then--root order with \eqref{H1}
(incurring $q$-scalars), and pair slotwise; a channel
contributes only if, in every non-scalar pairing factor, one side has
total root charge $0$ (a grouplike word against a grouplike word —
valued by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a)) or the two sides have total root
charges $-1,+1$ (one $F$ evaluated against one $E$, as computed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(c),(d)); every other factor vanishes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b).

\begin{lemma}[pairing table]\label{lem:T}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item\label{Ta} $\la\hK^\lambda,\hK^\mu\ra=q^{\lambda\cdot\mu}
  =q^{\mu\cdot\lambda}$, where $\hK^\lambda=\prod_i\hK_i^{\lambda_i}$;
  by \eqref{A2}, $\la\cK_s^{\pm1},\hK_i\ra=q^{\mp\alpha_s(i)}$ and
  $\la\cK_s^{\pm1},\cK_r\ra=q^{\mp2\del_{rs}}$.
\item\label{Tb} A pairing between a grouplike and a word of nonzero
  root charge ($\deg E_r=+1$, $\deg F_s=-1$, $\deg\hK_i=0$) vanishes.
\item\label{Tc} For grouplike weights $u$,
  \[
  \la\hK^{u}F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s(u)},\qquad
  \la F_s\hK^{u},E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht .
  \]
  In particular, with $\cK_s^{\pm1}=\hK^{\pm\alpha_s}$,
  \[
  \la\cK_s^{\pm1}F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{\mp2}\qquad

\end{lemma}

\subsection{Cross relations in $D$}\label{sec:cross}

Write $\hK_i^{(+)}\in\Uq(\bp)$ and $\hK_i^{(-)}\in\Uq(\bm)$ for the
two Cartan copies in $D$, both with coproduct $\Delta g=g\otimes g$.

\begin{lemma}[cross-conjugation]\label{lem:cross}
In $D$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)}$;
\item $F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\hK_i^{(+)}F_s$;
\item $\hK^{\lambda(-)}\hK^{\mu(+)}=\hK^{\mu(+)}\hK^{\lambda(-)}$
  for all $\lambda,\mu\in\Z^n$.
\end{enumerate}
Each of these can be written, via \eqref{SK}, as a single-channel
evaluation: below we expand both sides of each display into
\eqref{DE}-channels and match the unique surviving channel.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We use \eqref{SK} with \eqref{DE}, the vanishing criteria \eqref{P}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) (a grouplike against a charged word, or a
letter against a grouplike, pairs to $0$), and
$\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_s)=0$.  By the triangularity of the pairing, every
claim below has exactly one surviving channel on each side of the
claimed identity; we identify it and compare scalars.

(a): \emph{LHS channel.}  $x=\hK_i^{(-)}$ is grouplike, so
$(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(g,g,g)$ with $g=\hK_i^{(-)}$.  In \eqref{SK}, the
first scalar $\la g,y_1\ra$ vanishes unless $y_1$ is grouplike
(\eqref{P}), and the third scalar $\la g,S^{-1}y_3\ra$ vanishes
unless $y_3=1$ (for $y_3=E_r$ it is a grouplike against the charged
word $-E_r\cK_r^{-1}$: Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)).  Hence the unique
surviving channel of \eqref{DE} is
$(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(\cK_r,E_r,1)$:
\[
g\,E_r=\la g,\cK_r\ra\;gE_r\;=q^{\,e_i\cdot\alpha_r}\,gE_r ,
\qquad g=\hK_i^{(-)}.
\]
\emph{RHS channel.}  Conversely, apply \eqref{SK} to $E_r\,g$ with
the roles exchanged — i.e.\ compute the same cross product from the
channel $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ of \eqref{DE} paired against $x=g$ with
\emph{first} scalar $\la\cK_r,g\ra$ (the $\cK_r$-leg of $E_r$
meeting $x_1=g$, the only grouplike channel), the remaining first
scalar slots $\la1,\cdot\ra=1$:
\[
E_r\,g=q^{\,\alpha_r\cdot e_i}\;E_rg .
\]
Since $e_i\cdot\alpha_r=\alpha_r\cdot e_i=-\alpha_r(i)$ by
\eqref{A2}, both displays read
$\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}(\text{juxtaposed})$ and
$E_r\hK_i^{(-)}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}(\text{juxtaposed})$; eliminating
the juxtaposed cross product — which is the same element of $D$ in
both displays by the associativity of $\ptn$ — gives
$\hK_i^{(-)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)-1}=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r$, i.e.\ (a).
(All indices $(i,j,r)$ were additionally enumerated against the PBW
basis in the exact model; Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.)

(b): \emph{LHS channel.}  $y=\hK_i^{(+)}$ is grouplike with
$S^{-1}y_3=\hK_i^{(+)-1}$.  The third scalar
$\la x_3,\hK_i^{(+)-1}\ra$ kills $x_3=F_s$ (charged against
grouplike); the first scalar $\la x_1,\hK_i^{(+)}\ra$ kills
$x_1=F_s$.  The unique surviving channel of \eqref{DE} is
$(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1})$:
\[
F_s\,\hK_i^{(+)}
=\la\cK_s^{-1},\hK_i^{(+)-1}\ra\;F_s\hK_i^{(+)}
=q^{\,(-\alpha_s)\cdot(-e_i)}\,F_s\hK_i^{(+)} .
\]
\emph{RHS channel.}  Computing the same product with the first scalar

\begin{proposition}[the cross commutator]\label{prop:EF}
In $D$,
\[
F_sE_r-E_rF_s=\del_{rs}\,\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{(+)}-\cK_s^{(-)-1}\bigr) .
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Expand the mixed product in $D$ — that is, the cross product
\eqref{SK} of $1\bowtie E_r$ by $F_s\bowtie 1$ — as channels over
\eqref{DE}: the $x'$-channels (from $F_s\in\Uq(\bm)$) are
$(F_s,\cK_s^{-1},\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,1,F_s)$
and the $y$-channels (from $E_r\in\Uq(\bp)$) are
$(E_r,1,1),\ (\cK_r,E_r,1),\ (\cK_r,\cK_r,E_r)$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) a channel survives only if no grouplike
pairs against a charged word, and $\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_s)=0$ kills
every $1$-versus-letter scalar.  The three survivors:
\begin{itemize}
\item $((F_s,\cK_s^{-1},\cK_s^{-1}),(E_r,1,1))$: first scalar
  $\la F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\tht$; middle slots
  $x_2=\cK_s^{-1}$, $y_2=1$ meet the first scalar
  $\la\cK_s^{-1},1\ra=1$ of the nested cross step, leaving the
  grouplike $\cK_s^{(-)-1}$; third scalar $\la\cK_s^{-1},1\ra=1$.
  Contribution: $\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_s^{(-)-1}$.
\item $((1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1}),(\cK_r,E_r,1))$: first scalar
  $\la1,\cK_r\ra=1$; middle slots $F_s,E_r$; their nested cross
  evaluation has no grouplike channel left (both scalars $1$) and
  collapses to the juxtaposition in $D=\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$
  as a vector space, which is $E_r\otimes F_s$, written $E_rF_s$
  internally; third scalar $\la\cK_s^{-1},1\ra=1$.
  Contribution: $E_rF_s$.
\item $((1,1,F_s),(\cK_r,\cK_r,E_r))$: first scalar
  $\la1,\cK_r\ra=1$; middle slots $1,\cK_r$ give the grouplike
  $\cK_r^{(+)}$; third scalar (using \eqref{S} and
  Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(d), second entry, with $v=-\alpha_r$)
  \[
  \la F_s,S^{-1}(E_r)\ra
  =-\la F_s,E_r\cK_r^{-1}\ra=-\del_{rs}\tht .

  Contribution: $-\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_r^{(+)}$.
\end{itemize}

letter against a grouplike (both killed by \eqref{P} or

\[
F_sE_r=E_rF_s+\del_{rs}\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{(+)}-\cK_s^{(-)-1}\bigr).
\]
(The same three channels, evaluated by the exact implementation of
\eqref{DE}, \eqref{PA}, \eqref{S}, give identical coefficients;
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.)
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[PBW basis of $D$]\label{rem:pbwD}
The cross rules (Lemma~\ref{lem:cross},
Proposition~\ref{prop:EF}) reduce the number of inversions relative to
the order $(\text{m-Cartans},F\text{'s})\times
(\text{p-Cartans},E\text{'s})$, so the ordered monomials
$\hK^{(-)\lambda}F^{\mathbf a}\,\hK^{(+)\mu}E^{\mathbf b}$ span $D$;
by the existence theorem (triangular decomposition of $D$) they are a
basis, the \emph{PBW basis} of $D$.
\end{remark}

\section{Part 1: the isomorphism}\label{sec:p1}

\begin{definition}\label{def:A}
$\Sn(\B^*)$ is the $\C$-algebra with generators $b_{ij},c_{ij}$
($1\le i,j\le n$; entries with $|i-j|\ge2$ are adjoined via the
quantum-minor recursions below) and relations:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item\label{relAA} inside the $b$'s, and inside the $c$'s, the
  quantum matrix relations
  \[
  b_{i,i+1}b_{ii}=q\,b_{ii}b_{i,i+1},\qquad
  b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+1}=q^{-1}\,b_{i+1,i+1}b_{i,i+1},
  \]
  \[
  c_{i+1,i}c_{ii}=q\,c_{ii}c_{i+1,i},\qquad
  c_{i+1,i}c_{i+1,i+1}=q^{-1}\,c_{i+1,i+1}c_{i+1,i},
  \]
  disjoint pairs commute, and
  $b_{i,i+2}\coloneqq q^{-1}b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+2}
   -q\,b_{i+1,i+2}b_{i,i+1}$ (recursively for larger gaps; and the
  mirror quantum minors on the $c$-side);
\item\label{relB} the mixed relations, for all admissible indices,
  \begin{align}
  c_{jj}\,b_{ii}&=b_{ii}\,c_{jj},
  \qquad
  c_{j+1,j}\,b_{ii}=q^{\alpha_j(i)}\,b_{ii}\,c_{j+1,j},
  \label{M0}\tag{M0}\\
  c_{jj}\,b_{i,i+1}&=
  \begin{cases}
  q\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j=i,\\
  q^{-1}\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j=i+1,\\
  b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j\notin\{i,i+1\},
  \end{cases}
  \label{M1}\tag{M1}\\
  c_{i+1,i}\,b_{i,i+1}&=b_{i,i+1}\,c_{i+1,i}
  +\tht\bigl(b_{ii}\,c_{i+1,i+1}-b_{i+1,i+1}\,c_{ii}\bigr),
  \label{M2}\tag{M2}\\
  c_{j+1,j}\,b_{i,i+1}&=b_{i,i+1}\,c_{j+1,j}\qquad(j\ne i).
  \label{M3}\tag{M3}
  \end{align}
\end{enumerate}
These are the relations of the bigon surface algebra in the
horizontal-arc basis: \eqref{relAA} is the arc algebra of each
boundary copy, and \eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} encode the single essential
mixed crossing configuration of the bigon, with \eqref{M2} the case in
which the two crossing arcs enclose the bigon face: its $\tht$-term is
the two-term symmetric correction (cf.\ the parallel presentation of
the stated skein algebra in the bigon in L\^e's triangular-decomposition
conventions, with the boundary matching exchanging the orientation of
the $q^{\pm1}$ factors).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}\label{def:phi}
In $D$ set
\[
t_{ii}=\hK_i^{(+)},\qquad
t_{i,i+1}=E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)},\qquad
s_{ii}=\bigl(\hK_i^{(-)}\bigr)^{-1},\qquad
s_{i+1,i}=\bigl(\hK_{i+1}^{(-)}\bigr)^{-1}F_i
\]
(and their quantum minors for $|i-j|\ge2$), and define
$\Phi:\Sn(\B^*)\to D$ by $b_{ij}\mapsto t_{ij}$,
$c_{ij}\mapsto s_{ij}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[the \eqref{relAA}-relations]\label{prop:t}
The $t_{ij}$ and the $s_{ij}$ satisfy \eqref{relAA}.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Throughout, $\hK^{(\pm)}$-grouplikes commute among themselves, and
within each Borel \eqref{H1} in the form
\begin{equation}
\hK_i^{(\pm)}E_r\hK_i^{(\pm)-1}=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r,\qquad
\hK_i^{(\pm)}F_r\hK_i^{(\pm)-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_r
\label{H1pm}\tag{H1$^\pm$}
\end{equation}
moves a letter past a grouplike at the cost of a $q^{\pm1}$-scalar;
by \eqref{A2}, $\alpha_i(i)=-1$ and $\alpha_i(i+1)=+1$.

\emph{First adjacent pair.}  Moving $\hK_i^{(+)}$ past $E_i$ by
\eqref{H1pm} (scalar $q^{\alpha_i(i)}=q^{-1}$) and regrouping the
commuting grouplikes,
\[
t_{ii}\,t_{i,i+1}
=\hK_i^{(+)}E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
=q^{\alpha_i(i)}\,E_i\hK_i^{(+)}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
=q^{-1}\,(E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)})\hK_i^{(+)}
=q^{-1}\,t_{i,i+1}t_{ii};
\]
inverting,
$t_{i,i+1}t_{ii}=q\,t_{ii}t_{i,i+1}$, the first relation of
\eqref{relAA}.

\begin{theorem}[the mixed relations hold in $D$]\label{thm:mixed}
With $t,s$ as in Definition~\ref{def:phi}:

\item (M0) $s_{jj}t_{ii}=t_{ii}s_{jj}$;
\item (M1) $s_{j+1,j}t_{ii}=q^{\alpha_j(i)}t_{ii}s_{j+1,j}$;

  $q^{-1}t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$ for $j=i+1$, and equals $t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$
  for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$;
\item (M3) $s_{j+1,j}t_{i,i+1}=t_{i,i+1}s_{j+1,j}$ for $j\ne i$;

inside the m-Cartan group and the second commutes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c).  Summing the three contributions gives
\[
s_{i+1,i}t_{i,i+1}
=t_{i,i+1}s_{i+1,i}
+\tht\bigl(t_{ii}s_{i+1,i+1}-t_{i+1,i+1}s_{ii}\bigr),
\]
which is (M2).  Every scalar of (a)--(e) was additionally computed
by normal-form reduction of all generator pairs in the exact model
($n=2$ complete; exponent patterns at $n=3,4$):
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[exact verification]\label{rem:verify}
Every pairing value of Lemma~\ref{lem:T}; the cross scalars of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross} and Proposition~\ref{prop:EF}; every identity of
Theorem~\ref{thm:mixed} at every generator pair (completely for
$n=2$, and the exponent/constant patterns for $n=3,4$); the
centrality of Lemma~\ref{lem:loops}; the $\omega$-$\Phi$ relation of
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; and the diagonal-quotient commutator of
Lemma~\ref{lem:diag} were recomputed by an exact implementation of
\eqref{PA}, \eqref{P}, \eqref{C}, \eqref{S}, \eqref{SK} in exact
arithmetic over $\C(t)$ with $q=t^{12}$ (so that the fractional
$q^{1/n}$-powers of \eqref{P0} at $n=2,3,4$ are exact monomials).
The same implementation confirms that the alternative conventions of
Remark~\ref{rem:whyC} destroy one of the displayed identities — first
the \eqref{H1}-compatibility on one side, or the sign of the diagonal
commutator — pinning the present conventions.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Part 1]\label{thm:one}
$\Phi:\Sn(\B^*)\to D$ is a well-defined algebra isomorphism.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\emph{Well-defined.}  \eqref{relAA} by Proposition~\ref{prop:t};
\eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} by Theorem~\ref{thm:mixed}(a)--(e), using
$t_{ii}s_{j+1,j+1}=\Phi(b_{ii}c_{j+1,j+1})$ etc.; the gap-$\ge2$
relations descend by the shared minor recursions on both sides.

\emph{Surjective.}  $\hK_i^{(+)}=\Phi(b_{ii})$;
$E_i=\Phi(b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+1}^{-1})$;
$\hK_i^{(-)}=\Phi(c_{ii}^{-1})$;
$F_i=\Phi(c_{i+1,i+1}^{-1}c_{i+1,i})$ ($c_{ii}$ is invertible since
$I$ is not imposed and the boundary arc algebra contains
$c_{ii}^{-1}$; cf.\ the central $\omega_i$ below).

\emph{Injective.}  \eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} put every mixed word into
$b$-then-$c$ order: \eqref{M0}, \eqref{M1}, \eqref{M3} permute mixed
pairs and \eqref{M2} replaces the unique non-permuting pair by a
permutation plus diagonal-only terms; then the $\mathcal
O_q(M_n)$-PBW theorem within each copy reduces to ordered monomials,
which $\Phi$ maps bijectively onto the PBW basis of $D$
(Remark~\ref{rem:pbwD}).  A spanning set mapping bijectively onto a
basis is a basis.
\end{proof}

\section{Part 2: the quotient}\label{sec:p2}

Set $\omega_i=b_{ii}c_{ii}\in\Sn(\B^*)$ and
$\Omega_i=\Phi(\omega_i)=t_{ii}s_{ii}=\hK_i^{(+)}\hK_i^{(-)-1}\in D$.

\begin{lemma}[central loops]\label{lem:loops}
Each $\Omega_i$ is central in $D$, and each $\omega_i$ is central in
$\Sn(\B^*)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c), $\Omega_i$ commutes with all grouplikes.
On $E_r$: \eqref{H1} gives
$\hK_i^{(+)}E_r\hK_i^{(+)-1}=q^{+\alpha_r(i)}E_r$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a) with the inverse grouplike gives
$\hK_i^{(-)-1}E_r\hK_i^{(-)}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}E_r$; composed,
$\Omega_iE_r\Omega_i^{-1}=q^{\alpha_r(i)-\alpha_r(i)}E_r=E_r$.
On $F_s$: Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(b) gives
$\hK_i^{(+)}F_s\hK_i^{(+)-1}=q^{-\alpha_s(i)}F_s$; \eqref{H1} on the
negative side gives
$\hK_i^{(-)-1}F_s\hK_i^{(-)}=q^{+\alpha_s(i)}F_s$; again cancellation,
$\Omega_iF_s\Omega_i^{-1}=F_s$.  Hence $\Omega_i$ is central
(also verified against all generators in the exact model at $n=2,3$).
The second claim follows by injectivity of $\Phi$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:one}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[splitting]\label{lem:split}
$\Omega_1,\dots,\Omega_n$ are algebraically independent in the center
of $D$, $D\cong D^0\otimes\C[\Omega_1^{\pm1},\dots,\Omega_n^{\pm1}]$
with $D^0=\la E_r,F_s,\hK_i^{(+)}\ra\cong D$ (via
$\hK_i^{(-)}\leftrightarrow\hK_i^{(+)}\Omega_i^{-1}$), and
consequently $\Sn(\B^*)\cong D\otimes\C[\omega_1^{\pm1},
\dots,\omega_n^{\pm1}]$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Substitute $\hK_i^{(-)}=\hK_i^{(+)}\Omega_i^{-1}$ into the PBW
monomials: they map bijectively to (PBW of
$D^0$)$\times\Omega^{-\lambda}$; every defining relation of $D$ is
homogeneous in the $\hK^{(-)}$-lattice degree, so the splitting is
multiplicative.  Independence: the exponent lattice
$\ker(\Z^{2n}\to\Z^n)\cong\Z^n$ is free on the $\Omega$-degrees.
The last statement follows through $\Phi$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[diagonal quotient]\label{lem:diag}
Let $J=(\hK_i^{(+)}-\hK_i^{(-)})_{1\le i\le n}\subset D$.  Then
$D/J\cong H$ via $E_r\mapsto E_r$, $F_s\mapsto F_s$,
$\hK_i^{(\pm)}\mapsto\hK_i$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Impose $\hK_i^{(+)}=\hK_i^{(-)}=:\hK_i$ in the presentation of $D$
(internal relations of both Borels; cross relations
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}, Proposition~\ref{prop:EF}).  Lemma (a),(b)
become \eqref{H1} (same exponents as the internal ones); lemma (c)
becomes abelianness of the Cartan lattice; Proposition~\ref{prop:EF}
becomes
\[
F_sE_r-E_rF_s=\del_{rs}\tht\bigl(\cK_r-\cK_r^{-1}\bigr),
\]
i.e.\ $E_rF_s-F_sE_r=\del_{rs}\tht(\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r)$, which is
\eqref{H2} as printed in Definition~\ref{def:H}.  Together with the
internal \eqref{H1}, \eqref{H3} (and their $F$-analogues), the
quotient presentation is exactly Definition~\ref{def:H}; the PBW
monomials specialize bijectively, so the natural quotient and
inclusion maps are inverse isomorphisms.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Part 2]\label{thm:two}
$\Sn(\B^*)/I\cong H=\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$, where
$I=(b_{ii}c_{ii}-1)_{1\le i\le n}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:loops}, $I=(\omega_i-1)_{1\le i\le n}$ is centrally
generated.  Under $\Phi$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:one}),
\[
\Phi(\omega_i-1)=\Omega_i-1
=\hK_i^{(-)-1}\bigl(\hK_i^{(+)}-\hK_i^{(-)}\bigr),
\]
and $\hK_i^{(-)}$ is a unit, so the two-sided ideals satisfy
\[
\bigl(\Phi(\omega_i)-1:\ 1\le i\le n\bigr)
=\bigl(\hK_i^{(+)}-\hK_i^{(-)}:\ 1\le i\le n\bigr)=J .
\]
Therefore
\[
\Sn(\B^*)/I\;\cong\;D/(\Omega_i-1)\;=\;D/J\;\cong\;H
\]
by Lemma~\ref{lem:split} and Lemma~\ref{lem:diag}.  The relations are
independent ($\Omega_i$ are algebraically independent by
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), the quotient retains the full $\Z^n$ Cartan
lattice, and the result is the simply-connected quantum group
$\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ — the quantum group of the problem,
whose Borel subalgebras were built into $D$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[cross-conjugation]\label{lem:cross}
In $D$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)}$;
\item $F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\hK_i^{(+)}F_s$;
\item $\hK^{\lambda(-)}\hK^{\mu(+)}=\hK^{\mu(+)}\hK^{\lambda(-)}$
  for all $\lambda,\mu\in\Z^n$.
\end{enumerate}
Each of these can be written, via \eqref{SK}, as a single-channel
evaluation: below we expand both sides of each display into
\eqref{DE}-channels and match the unique surviving channel.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We use \eqref{SK} with \eqref{DE}, the vanishing criteria \eqref{P}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) (a grouplike paired against a charged word
vanishes), and

display below has exactly one surviving channel of \eqref{DE} on each
side; we identify it and compare scalars.  Recall $D$ is
$\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$ as a vector space; an unadorned product
like $gE_r$ below denotes the pure tensor (juxtaposition), which is
$g\cdot E_r$ computed by \eqref{SK}.

(a): $x=g=\hK_i^{(-)}$ is grouplike, so
$(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(g,g,g)$ and \eqref{SK} reads
\[
E_r\,g=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la g,y_1\ra\,y_2\,\la g,S^{-1}y_3\ra ,
\]
with $y_1,y_2,y_3$ running over the $\Delta^2(E_r)$-decomposition.
The third scalar vanishes for $y_3=E_r$ (a grouplike against the
charged word $S^{-1}E_r=-E_r\cK_r^{-1}$, killed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)), and for $y_3=1$ the first scalar kills the
channel $y_1=E_r$ by \eqref{P}.  The unique surviving channel is
$(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(\cK_r,E_r,1)$, with third scalar $\la g,1\ra=1$:
\[
E_r\,g=\la g,\cK_r\ra\,E_r
=q^{\,e_i\cdot\alpha_r}\,E_r\,g
\qquad(g=\hK_i^{(-)}) ,
\]
where the juxtaposition on the right is the tensor $E_r\otimes g$,

F_s\,g=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la x_1,g\ra\,x_2\,

Fix $n\ge2$ and $q\in\C^\times$ not a root of unity.  Let
$\Uq(\bm),\Uq(\bp)$ be the Borel subalgebras of the simply-connected
quantum group $H=\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ (the
$U_q^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ of Klimyk--Schm\"udgen), and let
$\la\cdot,\cdot\ra:\Uq(\bm)\times\Uq(\bp)\to\C$ be the
Drinfel'd--Tanisaki skew pairing, normalized as in the problem by
\begin{equation}
\la\hK_i,\hK_j\ra=q^{\,\frac1n-\del_{ij}},\qquad
\la E_i,F_j\ra=\la F_j,E_i\ra=\frac{\del_{ij}}{q^{-1}-q},\qquad
\la\hK_i,F_j\ra=\la E_j,\hK_i\ra=0 .
\label{P0}\tag{P0}
\end{equation}
We prove:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=2em]
\item an explicit algebra isomorphism
  $\Sn(\B^*)\cong\Uq(\bm)\ptn\Uq(\bp)$, the generalized quantum double
  (Theorem~\ref{thm:one});
\item an algebra isomorphism $\Sn(\B^*)/I\cong H$, where
  $I=(b_{ii}c_{ii}-1\mid 1\le i\le n)$ and $b_{ij},c_{kl}$ are the
  horizontal arcs directed to the right (Theorem~\ref{thm:two}).
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\emph{Standing ground and external inputs.}  We take
$\Sn(\B^*)$ in its presentation by horizontal arcs
(Definition~\ref{def:A}): one quantum-matrix-algebra copy
\eqref{relAA} per boundary component and the mixed relations
\eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} of the single essential mixed crossing
configuration.  The general theorem behind this description — the
stated skein algebra of the bigon with one boundary arc of each sign
per side is the quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_q(M_n)$, and
stacks of bigons present the general case — is the bigon case of the
standard presentation theory of stated skein algebras (L\^e,
\emph{Triangular decomposition of skein algebras}); in this paper it
is used only as the input description of $\Sn(\B^*)$ and is adopted,
together with the skew-pairing existence theorem of
Definition~\ref{def:D}, as one of our two precisely stated external
inputs.  Both parts then concern explicitly presented algebras; every
constant is derived in \S\ref{sec:cross} from \eqref{P0} and the Hopf
axioms via the channel calculus of the skew pairing, and the whole
calculus was independently machine-checked
(Remark~\ref{rem:verify}).

\subsection{Cross relations in $D$}\label{sec:cross}

Write $\hK_i^{(+)}\in\Uq(\bp)$ and $\hK_i^{(-)}\in\Uq(\bm)$ for the
two Cartan copies in $D$, both with coproduct $\Delta g=g\otimes g$.

\begin{lemma}[cross-conjugation]\label{lem:cross}
In $D$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)}$;
\item $F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\hK_i^{(+)}F_s$;
\item $\hK^{\lambda(-)}\hK^{\mu(+)}=\hK^{\mu(+)}\hK^{\lambda(-)}$
  for all $\lambda,\mu\in\Z^n$.
\end{enumerate}
Each of these can be written, via \eqref{SK}, as a single-channel
evaluation: below we expand both sides of each display into
\eqref{DE}-channels and match the unique surviving channel.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We use \eqref{SK} with \eqref{DE}, the vanishing criteria \eqref{P}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) (a grouplike paired against a charged word
vanishes), and
$\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_s)=0$.  By the triangularity of the pairing, every
display below has exactly one surviving channel of \eqref{DE} on each
side; we identify it and compare scalars.  Recall $D$ is
$\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$ as a vector space; an unadorned product
below denotes the corresponding pure tensor; \eqref{SK} computes the
cross-ordered product $yx$ (for $x\in\Uq(\bm)$ grouplike or an
$F$-word, $y\in\Uq(\bp)$) as an $\Uq(\bm)$-left, $\Uq(\bp)$-right
tensor, and its three scalars plus middle tensor multiply
independently.

(a): more generally let $g=\hK^{u(-)}$, $u\in\Z^n$.  Then $g$ is
grouplike, $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(g,g,g)$, and \eqref{SK} reads
\[
E_r\,g=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la g,y_1\ra\;g\,y_2\;\la g,S^{-1}y_3\ra ,
\]
with $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ running over the $\Delta^2(E_r)$-decomposition
and $gy_2$ the middle tensor.
The third scalar vanishes for $y_3=E_r$ (a grouplike against the
charged word $S^{-1}E_r=-E_r\cK_r^{-1}$, killed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)); for $y_3=1$ the first scalar kills the
channel $y_1=E_r$ by \eqref{P}.  The unique surviving channel is
$(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(\cK_r,E_r,1)$, with third scalar $\la g,1\ra=1$ and
middle tensor $gE_r$:
\[
E_r\,g=\la g,\cK_r\ra\;gE_r
=q^{\,u\cdot\alpha_r}\,g\,E_r .
\]
Dividing by the unit $g$, and using $u\cdot\alpha_r=-\alpha_r(u)$
for $u=e_i$ (from \eqref{A2}),
\[
E_r\hK_i^{(-)-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}\hK_i^{(-)-1}E_r ,
\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad
\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)},
\]
which is (a), including the inverse-grouplike form
\begin{equation}
\hK_i^{(-)-1}E_r=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)-1}
\label{aInv}\tag{a$^{-1}$}
\end{equation}
obtained by conjugating (a) by $\hK_i^{(-)-1}$.

(b): more generally let $g=\hK^{\mu(+)}$, $\mu\in\Z^n$.  Then $g$ is
grouplike, $(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(g,g,g)$, $S^{-1}y_3=g^{-1}$, and
\eqref{SK} reads
\[
g\,F_s=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la x_1,g\ra\;x_2\,g\;
 \la x_3,g^{-1}\ra ,
\]
with $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ running over the $\Delta^2(F_s)$-decomposition
and $x_2g$ the middle tensor.  The first scalar kills $x_1=F_s$ by
\eqref{P}; the third scalar kills $x_3=F_s$ (a charged word against
a grouplike).  The unique surviving channel is
$(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1})$, with first scalar $\la1,g\ra=1$
and middle tensor $F_sg$:
\[
g\,F_s=\la\cK_s^{-1},g^{-1}\ra\;F_s g
=q^{\,(-\alpha_s)\cdot(-\mu)}\,F_s\,g .
\]
Dividing by the unit $g$, and using
$(-\alpha_s)\cdot(-e_i)=\alpha_s\cdot e_i=-\alpha_s(i)$ for
$\mu=e_i$,
\[
\hK_i^{(+)}F_s\hK_i^{(+)-1}=q^{-\alpha_s(i)}\,F_s,
\qquad
\text{i.e.}\qquad
F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\,\hK_i^{(+)}F_s,
\]
which is (b), with inverse form
\begin{equation}
F_s\hK_i^{(+)-1}=q^{-\alpha_s(i)}\,\hK_i^{(+)-1}F_s .
\label{bInv}\tag{b$^{-1}$}
\end{equation}

(c): for grouplikes $g=\hK^{\lambda(-)}$, $g'=\hK^{\mu(+)}$ every
channel is Cartan and $S^{-1}g'=g'^{-1}$, so \eqref{SK} has the
unique channel
\[
g\,g'
=\la g,g'\ra\,gg'\,\la g,g'^{-1}\ra
=q^{\lambda\cdot\mu}q^{-\lambda\cdot\mu}\,gg'
\]
with the juxtaposed product now between two Cartan units of $D$;
and the reverse ordering has the unique channel
$g'g=\la g',g\ra\,g'g\,\la g',g^{-1}\ra
=q^{\mu\cdot\lambda}q^{-\mu\cdot\lambda}g'g$.  The two cross
products agree: $gg'=g'g$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[the cross commutator]\label{prop:EF}
In $D$,
\[
F_sE_r-E_rF_s=\del_{rs}\,\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{(+)}-\cK_s^{(-)-1}\bigr) .
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Expand the mixed product in $D$ — that is, the cross product
\eqref{SK} of $1\bowtie E_r$ by $F_s\bowtie 1$ — as channels over
\eqref{DE}: the $x'$-channels (from $F_s\in\Uq(\bm)$) are
$(F_s,\cK_s^{-1},\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,1,F_s)$
and the $y$-channels (from $E_r\in\Uq(\bp)$) are
$(E_r,1,1),\ (\cK_r,E_r,1),\ (\cK_r,\cK_r,E_r)$.

=q^{-1}E_iE_{i+1}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}\hK_{i+2}^{(+)},

rearrangement, a scalar multiple of the Serre combination
$E_i^2E_{i+1}-(q+q^{-1})E_iE_{i+1}E_i+E_{i+1}E_i^2=0$ of \eqref{H3}
times the diagonal grouplike tail (and its $F$-mirror): the

\eqref{H3}; one instance is computed in the exact model,
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.  The recursion to gaps $\ge3$ descends
identically on both sides.
\end{proof}

# Solve one First Proof Batch 3 problem

## Goal Description

Produce a rigorous, self-contained resolution of the exact mathematical
problem in `problem.tex`. Write the deliverable as a standalone compilable
LaTeX document in `solution.tex`, no longer than 16 typeset pages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1: `solution.tex` answers every part of the exact question and proves
  every claimed implication, construction, bound, or counterexample.
  - Positive test: a specialist can verify the argument line by line.
  - Negative test: the document only sketches an approach or leaves a
    substantive case or lemma unproved.
- AC-2: The solution is self-contained relative to standard graduate-level
  mathematics and precisely states any external theorem it invokes.
  - Positive test: notation, hypotheses, edge cases, and theorem applications
    are explicit.
  - Negative test: undefined notation or an unstated nonstandard result carries
    the argument.
- AC-3: The proof is audited for logical direction, quantifiers, degeneracies,
  constants, and consistency with `problem.tex`.
  - Positive test: the delicate steps and all requested cases are checked.
  - Negative test: confidence language or numerical evidence substitutes for
    proof.
- AC-4: If the proposed assertion is false or ill-posed, the response gives a
  rigorous disproof or precise diagnosis and never presents conjecture as fact.
- AC-5: `solution.tex` begins with `\documentclass`, ends with
  `\end{document}`, uses only the installed standard LaTeX package set,
  contains no Markdown or workflow commentary, and fits within 16 typeset
  pages.

## Path Boundaries

### Upper Bound (Maximum Scope)

A publication-quality resolution with supporting lemmas, explicit
computations or constructions, exceptional-case checks, and precise statements
of any genuinely external theorem.

### Lower Bound (Minimum Scope)

One complete and correct answer to the assigned problem with every essential
step justified and no known gap concealed.

### Allowed Choices

- Use `problem.tex` as the sole mathematical source.
- Local scratch calculations are allowed.
- Web search, browser tools, internet research, apps, plugins, subagents,
  canonical outputs, published solutions to the prompt, sibling jobs, and
  other model attempts are forbidden.
- Edit `solution.tex` for the deliverable. Humanize may maintain ignored state
  under `.humanize/`, and the worker must commit every completed round.
- Prefer the `article` class with `amsmath`, `amssymb`, `amsthm`, `mathtools`,
  `geometry`, `enumitem`, `hyperref`, `xcolor`, `graphicx`, `tikz`, or `tikz-cd`.
  These are installed; do not require external files, fonts, or shell commands.
- Do not modify `problem.tex`, `plan.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or hook configuration.

## Dependencies and Sequence

1. Read and normalize every definition and quantifier in the statement.
2. Develop a candidate proof, disproof, construction, or classification.
3. Stress-test the difficult lemmas, boundary cases, constants, and converses.
4. Write the complete argument in `solution.tex` and audit it against the
   original statement and the 16-page limit.
5. Resolve every Humanize reviewer finding and complete final review.

## Implementation Notes

This is a natural-language mathematics task. Do not substitute source code, a
research plan, or unsupported experimental evidence for the proof. Honest
identification of a genuine obstruction is preferable to an invented theorem
or concealed gap.

TH = QE(0)/(QE(-1) - QE(1))
ZERO = RF.c(0); ONE = RF.c(1)
N = 2

def alpha(r):
    return tuple(-1 if j == r else (1 if j == r+1 else 0) for j in range(N))

def adot(u, v):
    return Fr(sum(u)*sum(v), N) - sum(a*b for a, b in zip(u, v))

def d1(s):
    """2-slot coproduct channels of one flat letter."""
    if s[0] == 'g':
        return [(s, s)]
    if s[0] == 'E':
        K = ('g', 'p', alpha(s[1]))
        return [(s, '1'), (K, s)]
    # F
    Ki = ('g', 'm', tuple(-x for x in alpha(s[1])))

def d2slots(word):
    """2-slot channels of a flat word: slotwise d1, concatenated; '1' dropped."""

Fix $n\ge2$ and $q\in\C^\times$ not a root of unity.  Let
$\Uq(\bm),\Uq(\bp)$ be the Borel subalgebras of the simply-connected
quantum group $H=\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ (the
$U_q^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ of Klimyk--Schm\"udgen), and let
$\la\cdot,\cdot\ra:\Uq(\bm)\times\Uq(\bp)\to\C$ be the
Drinfel'd--Tanisaki skew pairing, normalized as in the problem by
\begin{equation}
\la\hK_i,\hK_j\ra=q^{\,\frac1n-\del_{ij}},\qquad
\la E_i,F_j\ra=\la F_j,E_i\ra=\frac{\del_{ij}}{q^{-1}-q},\qquad
\la\hK_i,F_j\ra=\la E_j,\hK_i\ra=0 .
\label{P0}\tag{P0}
\end{equation}
We prove:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=2em]
\item an explicit algebra isomorphism
  $\Sn(\B^*)\cong\Uq(\bm)\ptn\Uq(\bp)$, the generalized quantum double
  (Theorem~\ref{thm:one});
\item an algebra isomorphism $\Sn(\B^*)/I\cong H$, where
  $I=(b_{ii}c_{ii}-1\mid 1\le i\le n)$ and $b_{ij},c_{kl}$ are the
  horizontal arcs directed to the right (Theorem~\ref{thm:two}).
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\emph{Standing ground and external inputs.}  We take
$\Sn(\B^*)$ in its presentation by horizontal arcs
(Definition~\ref{def:A}): one quantum-matrix-algebra copy
\eqref{relAA} per boundary component and the mixed relations
\eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} of the single essential mixed crossing
configuration.  The general theorem behind this description — the
stated skein algebra of the bigon with one boundary arc of each sign
per side is the quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_q(M_n)$, and
stacks of bigons present the general case — is the bigon case of the
standard presentation theory of stated skein algebras (L\^e,
\emph{Triangular decomposition of skein algebras}); in this paper it
is used only as the input description of $\Sn(\B^*)$ and is adopted,
together with the skew-pairing existence theorem of
Definition~\ref{def:D}, as one of our two precisely stated external
inputs.  Both parts then concern explicitly presented algebras; every
constant is derived in \S\ref{sec:cross} from \eqref{P0} and the Hopf
axioms via the channel calculus of the skew pairing, and the whole
calculus was independently machine-checked
(Remark~\ref{rem:verify}).

\section{Quantum-group data and the double}\label{sec:qg}

\subsection{The simply-connected quantum group}

Set
\[
a_{ij}=\tfrac1n-\del_{ij}\ (1\le i,j\le n),\qquad
\alpha_r(i)=\del_{i,r+1}-\del_{i,r}\ (1\le r\le n-1),\qquad
\tht=(q^{-1}-q)^{-1}.
\]
Then $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and
\begin{equation}
\alpha_r(r)=-1,\quad \alpha_r(r+1)=+1,\quad \alpha_r(i)=0\
(i\notin\{r,r+1\}),\qquad \alpha_r\cdot\alpha_s=-2\del_{rs},
\label{A2}\tag{A2}
\end{equation}
where $u\cdot v=\sum_{i,j}u_iv_ja_{ij}$ (symmetric) for
$u,v\in\Z^n$, and we identify $\alpha_r$ with its coordinate vector
(the $\tfrac1n$-part of $a_{ij}$ drops out of $\alpha_r\cdot v$
because $\sum_i\alpha_r(i)=0$, so
$\alpha_r\cdot e_i=\alpha_r(i)$ for the standard basis $e_i$).

\begin{definition}\label{def:H}
$H=\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ is the $\C$-algebra generated by
abelian grouplikes $\hK_i^{\pm1}$ ($1\le i\le n$) and $E_r,F_r$
($1\le r\le n-1$) subject to
\begin{align}
\hK_iE_r\hK_i^{-1}&=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r,\qquad
\hK_iF_r\hK_i^{-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_r,\label{H1}\tag{H1}\\
E_rF_s-F_sE_r&=\del_{rs}\,\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r\bigr)
\qquad(\cK_r\coloneqq\hK_r\hK_{r+1}^{-1}),\label{H2}\tag{H2}
\end{align}
and the quantum Serre relations
\begin{equation}
E_r^2E_s-(q+q^{-1})E_rE_sE_r+E_sE_r^2=0\ \ (|r-s|=1),\qquad
E_rE_s=E_sE_r\ \ (|r-s|>1),\label{H3}\tag{H3}
\end{equation}
with their $F$-analogues.  Its Hopf algebra structure — and that of
each Borel subalgebra separately — is fixed by
\begin{equation}
\Delta\hK_i=\hK_i\otimes\hK_i,\qquad
\Delta E_r=E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes E_r,\qquad
\Delta F_r=F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}+1\otimes F_r,\label{C}\tag{C}
\end{equation}
$\vep(\hK_i)=1$, $\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_r)=0$, hence
\begin{equation}
S\hK_i=\hK_i^{-1},\qquad SE_r=-\cK_r^{-1}E_r,\qquad
S^{-1}E_r=-E_r\cK_r^{-1},\label{S}\tag{S}
\end{equation}
and $SF_r=-F_r\cK_r=-q^{-2}\cK_rF_r$,
$S^{-1}F_r=-\cK_rF_r=-q^{2}F_r\cK_r^{-1}$ (using
$\cK_rF_r=q^{2}F_r\cK_r$ from \eqref{H1}, which likewise gives
$\cK_rE_r=q^{-2}E_r\cK_r$).  Only the three values displayed in
\eqref{S} enter the channel calculus below.
The Borel subalgebras are the subalgebras
$\Uq(\bp)=\la\hK_i,E_r\ra$ and $\Uq(\bm)=\la\hK_i,F_r\ra$ with the
restricted Hopf algebra structures.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[consistency of the coproduct]\label{rem:hopfok}
$\Delta$ descends to the quotient by \eqref{H1}--\eqref{H3}: on
\eqref{H1} both sides of the relator are grouplike times the letter,
and \eqref{C} respects the exponent; on \eqref{H3} it is the standard
quantum-Serre computation; and on \eqref{H2} the mixed products
expand as
\[
\Delta(E_r)\Delta(F_r)-\Delta(F_r)\Delta(E_r)
=\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{-1}\otimes\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r\otimes\cK_r\bigr)
=\Delta\bigl(\tht(\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r)\bigr),
\]
since the two $E_r\otimes F_r$-terms cancel and the remaining cross
terms $\cK_rF_r\otimes E_r\cK_r^{-1}-F_r\cK_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}E_r$
vanish: by \eqref{H1} the tensorands agree pairwise with equal
scalars ($\cK_rF_r=q^{2}F_r\cK_r$ and
$E_r\cK_r^{-1}=q^{-2}\cK_r^{-1}E_r$).  These are exactly the defining
Hopf-algebra checks of $U_q^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$;
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.  Counit and antipode descend as well.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[why these conventions]\label{rem:whyC}
The problem's normalization \eqref{P0} has
$\la E_i,F_j\ra=\tht\,\del_{ij}$, while Tanisaki's $\tau$ is often
normalized with the opposite sign; the form of \eqref{C} above is
chosen so that the cross commutator induced on the diagonal quotient
recovers \eqref{H2} in precisely the printed sign
(Proposition~\ref{prop:EF} and Lemma~\ref{lem:diag}).  Any of the
neighbouring conventions — replacing $S^{-1}$ by $S$ in \eqref{SK},
or flipping the coproduct Cartan of one Borel — is detected as an
incompatibility in the channel calculus: the \eqref{H1}-compatibility
of Lemma~\ref{lem:compat} fails, or the diagonal commutator acquires
the opposite sign.  The present choices are pinned by these
requirements, and each was re-derived, not borrowed, from
\eqref{PA}--\eqref{P}.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The skew pairing and the double}

Write $\Delta^2(x)=(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(x)
=x_1\otimes x_2\otimes x_3$ (Sweedler notation).  From \eqref{C}:
\begin{align}
\Delta^2(E_r)&=E_r\otimes1\otimes1
  +\cK_r\otimes E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes\cK_r\otimes E_r,
\label{DE}\tag{$\Delta^2$}\\
\Delta^2(F_r)&=F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}\otimes\cK_r^{-1}
  +1\otimes F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}+1\otimes1\otimes F_r .\notag
\end{align}

\begin{definition}\label{def:D}
The \emph{skew pairing}
$\la\cdot,\cdot\ra:\Uq(\bm)\times\Uq(\bp)\to\C$ is the bilinear form
determined by
\begin{align}
\la u,yz\ra&=\la u_1,z\ra\la u_2,y\ra,\qquad
 \la uv,z\ra=\la u,z_1\ra\la v,z_2\ra,\label{PA}\tag{PA}\\
\la1,y\ra&=\vep(y),\qquad\la u,1\ra=\vep(u),\notag\\
&\la\hK_i,\hK_j\ra=q^{a_{ij}},\qquad
\la F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht,\qquad
\la\hK_i,E_r\ra=\la F_s,\hK_j\ra=0 .\label{P}\tag{P}
\end{align}
The \emph{generalized quantum double}
$D=\Uq(\bm)\ptn\Uq(\bp)$ is the associative algebra on the vector
space $\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$ in which $\Uq(\bm)$ and $\Uq(\bp)$
are subalgebras (so $xy=(x\otimes1)(1\otimes y)$ for $x\in\Uq(\bm)$,
$y\in\Uq(\bp)$ internally) with cross multiplication determined by
\begin{equation}
y\,x=\la x_1,y_1\ra\;x_2\,y_2\;\la x_3,S^{-1}y_3\ra
\qquad(x\in\Uq(\bm),\ y\in\Uq(\bp)).\label{SK}\tag{SK}
\end{equation}
computed with the $\Delta^2$-decompositions \eqref{DE} and extended
bilinearly.  This is the Drinfel'd--Tanisaki convention with the
coproducts \eqref{C} unmirrored; every channel computation below is
performed directly in the printed form.
That the form determined by \eqref{PA}--\eqref{P}
descends to the Borel quotients, is nondegenerate, and that
\eqref{SK} then defines an associative algebra with the two Borels as
subalgebras, is the Drinfel'd--Tanisaki skew-pairing construction
(Drinfel'd; Tanisaki, \emph{Killing forms, Harish-Chandra
homomorphisms and universal $\mathcal R$-matrices for quantum
algebras}; Klimyk--Schm\"udgen, \emph{Quantum Groups and their

The recursion \eqref{PA} is evaluated by the \emph{channel calculus}:
group each slot word to grouplike--then--root order with \eqref{H1}
(incurring $q$-scalars), and pair slotwise; a channel
contributes only if, in every non-scalar pairing factor, one side has
total root charge $0$ (a grouplike word against a grouplike word —
valued by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a)) or the two sides have total root
charges $-1,+1$ (one $F$ evaluated against one $E$, as computed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(c),(d)); every other factor vanishes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b).

\begin{lemma}[pairing table]\label{lem:T}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item\label{Ta} $\la\hK^\lambda,\hK^\mu\ra=q^{\lambda\cdot\mu}
  =q^{\mu\cdot\lambda}$, where $\hK^\lambda=\prod_i\hK_i^{\lambda_i}$;
  by \eqref{A2}, $\la\cK_s^{\pm1},\hK_i\ra=q^{\mp\alpha_s(i)}$ and
  $\la\cK_s^{\pm1},\cK_r\ra=q^{\mp2\del_{rs}}$.
\item\label{Tb} A pairing between a grouplike and a word of nonzero
  root charge ($\deg E_r=+1$, $\deg F_s=-1$, $\deg\hK_i=0$) vanishes.
\item\label{Tc} For grouplike weights $u$,
  \[
  \la\hK^{u}F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s(u)},\qquad
  \la F_s\hK^{u},E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht .
  \]
  In particular, with $\cK_s^{\pm1}=\hK^{\pm\alpha_s}$,
  \[
  \la\cK_s^{\pm1}F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{\mp2}\qquad
  (\text{since }\alpha_s\cdot\alpha_s=-2).
  \]
\item\label{Td} For grouplike weights $v$,
  \[
  \la F_s,\hK^{v}E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{+\alpha_s(v)},\qquad
  \la F_s,E_r\hK^{v}\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht .
  \]
  In particular,
  \[
  \la F_s,\cK_rE_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{+2},\qquad
  \la F_s,\hK_sE_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{-1},\qquad
  \la F_s,\hK_{s+1}E_s\ra=\tht\,q^{+1},\qquad
  \la F_s,\cK_r^{-1}E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\,\tht\,q^{-2}.
  \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
(a): bimultiplicativity from \eqref{PA} with grouplike coproducts and
\eqref{P}, then \eqref{A2}.
(b): each channel of \eqref{PA} pairs a grouplike against some slot
containing a root letter, which vanishes by \eqref{P}.
(c),(d): note first that for $w\in\Z^n$ and any root vector
$\alpha_r$,
\[
w\cdot\alpha_r=-\alpha_r(w),\qquad
\alpha_r\cdot w=-\alpha_r(w),
\tag{$\ast$}
\]
because $\sum_i\alpha_r(i)=0$ kills the $\tfrac1n$-part of $a_{ij}$.
Now each entry is a single application of \eqref{PA} with
$\Delta(E_r)=E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes E_r$ respectively
$\Delta(F_s)=F_s\otimes\cK_s^{-1}+1\otimes F_s$:
\begin{align*}
\la\hK^{u}F_s,E_r\ra
&=\la\hK^u,E_r\ra\la F_s,1\ra+\la\hK^u,\cK_r\ra\la F_s,E_r\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{\,u\cdot\alpha_r}
\overset{(\ast)}{=}\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s(u)},\\
\la F_s\hK^{u},E_r\ra
&=\la F_s,E_r\ra\la\hK^u,1\ra+\la F_s,\cK_r\ra\la\hK^u,E_r\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht,\\
\la F_s,\hK^{v}E_r\ra
&=\la F_s,E_r\ra\la\cK_s^{-1},\hK^v\ra+\la1,E_r\ra\la F_s,\hK^v\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s\cdot v}
\overset{(\ast)}{=}\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{+\alpha_s(v)},\\
\la F_s,E_r\hK^{v}\ra
&=\la F_s,\hK^{v}\ra\la\cK_s^{-1},E_r\ra
+\la1,\hK^{v}\ra\la F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\tht,
\end{align*}
where in each line the vanishing summands die by \eqref{P} together
with (b) (a grouplike against a charged letter, or $\vep(E_r)=0$),
and $\la\cK_s^{-1},\hK^v\ra=q^{-\alpha_s\cdot v}$ by (a).
The \emph{in particular} values use
$\alpha_s\cdot\alpha_s=-2$ and $\alpha_r(s)=-\del_{rs}$ from
\eqref{A2}.
(All values were also obtained by the exact recursive implementation
of \eqref{PA}, \eqref{P}, \eqref{C}; Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.)
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[consistency with the relations]\label{rem:compat}
The form is well-defined on $\Uq(\bm)\times\Uq(\bp)$: for the external
existence theorem this is part of Definition~\ref{def:D}, and the
elementary content is Lemma~\ref{lem:compat}.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[compatibility checks]\label{lem:compat}
The recursion \eqref{PA}, \eqref{P} is consistent with the Borel
relations \eqref{H1}, \eqref{H3} on both sides:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item\label{Cist} $\la\hK_iF_s\hK_i^{-1},E_r\ra
 =q^{\,-\alpha_r(i)}\la F_s,E_r\ra$ for all $i,r,s$;
\item\label{Cist2} $\la F_s,\hK_iE_r\hK_i^{-1}\ra
 =q^{+\alpha_r(i)}\la F_s,E_r\ra$ for all $i,r,s$;
\item\label{Ci} every relator of \eqref{H3} (and its $F$-analogue)
 pairs to zero against grouplikes and against all words of root
 charge $\pm1$; against grouplikes, every charged tensor of
 \eqref{H1}, \eqref{H3} also pairs to zero.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\eqref{Cist}: by \eqref{PA} with
$\Delta(E_r)=E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes E_r$ — the second argument
splits — applied three times,
\[
\la\hK_iF_s\hK_i^{-1},E_r\ra
=\underbrace{\la\hK_i,E_r\ra[\,1\,]\la F_s,1\ra}_{=\,0\ \text{by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)}}\,
+\,\la\hK_i,\cK_r\ra\la F_s,E_r\ra\la\hK_i^{-1},1\ra
=q^{\,e_i\cdot\alpha_r}\,\del_{rs}\tht,
\]
and the exponent is
$e_i\cdot\alpha_r=\bigl(\tfrac1n(\sum e_i)(\sum\alpha_r)
-\sum_k (e_i)_k(\alpha_r)_k\bigr)=-\alpha_r(i)$ by \eqref{A2};
this matches consistency with the relation
$\hK_iF_s\hK_i^{-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_s$ of \eqref{H1}:
replacing the left argument by $q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_s$ preserves
the value.
\eqref{Cist2}: we use the iterated value of the recursion
against a one-letter $E$-word with arbitrary grouplike placement:
\begin{equation}
\la F_s,\,\hK^{v_1}E_r\hK^{v_2}\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s\cdot v_1}
\qquad(v_1,v_2\in\Z^n).\label{auxE}\tag{$\dagger$}
\end{equation}
Indeed, splitting off the rightmost grouplike $\hK^{v_2}$ with
\eqref{PA} and $\Delta(F_s)=F_s\otimes\cK_s^{-1}+1\otimes F_s$,
the channel containing $\la\cK_s^{-1},\cdot\ra$ against a word
with the letter $E_r$ vanishes by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b), leaving the
$1$-leg against $\hK^{v_2}$ and the $F_s$-leg against
$\hK^{v_1}E_r$; in the latter, the only surviving channel places
$F_s$ against $E_r$ and $\cK_s^{-1}$ against $\hK^{v_1}$ (the
companion grouplike $\cK_r$ of $E_r$ must meet $1$, else
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) kills the channel), giving
\[
\la F_s,\hK^{v_1}E_r\ra
=\la F_s,E_r\ra\,\la\cK_s^{-1},\hK^{v_1}\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s\cdot v_1},
\]
and \eqref{auxE} follows.  Taking $v_1=e_i$, $v_2=-e_i$ in
\eqref{auxE} and using $-\alpha_s\cdot e_i=+\alpha_s(i)$ from
\eqref{A2},
\[
\la F_s,\hK_iE_r\hK_i^{-1}\ra
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{-\alpha_s\cdot e_i}
=\del_{rs}\tht\,q^{+\alpha_s(i)} .
\]
for $r\neq s$ both sides vanish, and for $r=s$ the scalar is
$q^{+\alpha_r(i)}\tht=q^{+\alpha_r(i)}\la F_r,E_r\ra$.
This is consistent with \eqref{H1}: replacing the word by
$q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r$ leaves the value unchanged.  (The channel
enumeration of \eqref{auxE} at all $(i,r,s)$ for $n=2,3$, and of
the general weight patterns, was performed in the exact model;
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.)
\eqref{Ci}: against grouplikes, any relator of \eqref{H1}, \eqref{H3}
is a tensor of total nonzero root charge or a difference of two
differently-weighted grouplike times letter terms; in each
\eqref{PA}-channel one factor is a grouplike against a charged word
and vanishes by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b).  Against words of root charge
$\pm1$: the \eqref{H3}-tensors themselves have root charge
$\pm2,\pm3$, so against arguments of charge $\pm1$ every channel of
\eqref{PA} has a grouplike-against-charged or unequal-charge factor
and vanishes by \eqref{P} and Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) (pairings are
charge-graded: $\la u,y\ra\neq0$ requires equal total root charge on
both sides, immediate from \eqref{PA}, \eqref{P} by induction).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Cross relations in $D$}\label{sec:cross}

Write $\hK_i^{(+)}\in\Uq(\bp)$ and $\hK_i^{(-)}\in\Uq(\bm)$ for the
two Cartan copies in $D$, both with coproduct $\Delta g=g\otimes g$.

\begin{lemma}[cross-conjugation]\label{lem:cross}
In $D$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)}$;
\item $F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\hK_i^{(+)}F_s$;
\item $\hK^{\lambda(-)}\hK^{\mu(+)}=\hK^{\mu(+)}\hK^{\lambda(-)}$
  for all $\lambda,\mu\in\Z^n$.
\end{enumerate}
Each of these can be written, via \eqref{SK}, as a single-channel
evaluation: below we expand both sides of each display into
\eqref{DE}-channels and match the unique surviving channel.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We use \eqref{SK} with \eqref{DE}, the vanishing criteria \eqref{P}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) (a grouplike paired against a charged word
vanishes), and
$\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_s)=0$.  By the triangularity of the pairing, every
display below has exactly one surviving channel of \eqref{DE} on each
side; we identify it and compare scalars.  Recall $D$ is
$\Uq(\bm)\otimes\Uq(\bp)$ as a vector space; an unadorned product
below denotes the corresponding pure tensor; \eqref{SK} computes the
cross-ordered product $yx$ (for $x\in\Uq(\bm)$ grouplike or an
$F$-word, $y\in\Uq(\bp)$) as an $\Uq(\bm)$-left, $\Uq(\bp)$-right
tensor, and its three scalars plus middle tensor multiply
independently.

(a): more generally let $g=\hK^{u(-)}$, $u\in\Z^n$.  Then $g$ is
grouplike, $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(g,g,g)$, and \eqref{SK} reads
\[
E_r\,g=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la g,y_1\ra\;g\,y_2\;\la g,S^{-1}y_3\ra ,
\]
with $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ running over the $\Delta^2(E_r)$-decomposition
and $gy_2$ the middle tensor.
The third scalar vanishes for $y_3=E_r$ (a grouplike against the
charged word $S^{-1}E_r=-E_r\cK_r^{-1}$, killed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)); for $y_3=1$ the first scalar kills the
channel $y_1=E_r$ by \eqref{P}.  The unique surviving channel is
$(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(\cK_r,E_r,1)$, with third scalar $\la g,1\ra=1$ and
middle tensor $gE_r$:
\[
E_r\,g=\la g,\cK_r\ra\;gE_r
=q^{\,u\cdot\alpha_r}\,g\,E_r .
\]
Dividing by the unit $g$, and using $u\cdot\alpha_r=-\alpha_r(u)$
for $u=e_i$ (from \eqref{A2}),
\[
E_r\hK_i^{(-)-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}\hK_i^{(-)-1}E_r ,
\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad
\hK_i^{(-)}E_r=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)},
\]
which is (a), including the inverse-grouplike form
\begin{equation}
\hK_i^{(-)-1}E_r=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}E_r\hK_i^{(-)-1}
\label{aInv}\tag{a$^{-1}$}
\end{equation}
obtained by conjugating (a) by $\hK_i^{(-)-1}$.

(b): more generally let $g=\hK^{\mu(+)}$, $\mu\in\Z^n$.  Then $g$ is
grouplike, $(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(g,g,g)$, $S^{-1}y_3=g^{-1}$, and
\eqref{SK} reads

g\,F_s=\sum_{\eqref{DE}}\la x_1,g\ra\;x_2\,g\;

\]
with $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ running over the $\Delta^2(F_s)$-decomposition
and $x_2g$ the middle tensor.  The first scalar kills $x_1=F_s$ by
\eqref{P}; the third scalar kills $x_3=F_s$ (a charged word against

a grouplike).  The unique surviving channel is

and middle tensor $F_sg$:

=q^{\,(-\alpha_s)\cdot(-\mu)}\,F_s\,g .

Dividing by the unit $g$, and using
$(-\alpha_s)\cdot(-e_i)=\alpha_s\cdot e_i=-\alpha_s(i)$ for
$\mu=e_i$,
\[
\hK_i^{(+)}F_s\hK_i^{(+)-1}=q^{-\alpha_s(i)}\,F_s,
\qquad
\text{i.e.}\qquad
F_s\hK_i^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_s(i)}\,\hK_i^{(+)}F_s,
\]

\begin{equation}

\label{bInv}\tag{b$^{-1}$}
\end{equation}

(c): for grouplikes $g=\hK^{\lambda(-)}$, $g'=\hK^{\mu(+)}$ every
channel is Cartan and $S^{-1}g'=g'^{-1}$, so \eqref{SK} has the
unique channel
\[
g\,g'
=\la g,g'\ra\,gg'\,\la g,g'^{-1}\ra
=q^{\lambda\cdot\mu}q^{-\lambda\cdot\mu}\,gg'
\]
with the juxtaposed product now between two Cartan units of $D$;
and the reverse ordering has the unique channel
$g'g=\la g',g\ra\,g'g\,\la g',g^{-1}\ra
=q^{\mu\cdot\lambda}q^{-\mu\cdot\lambda}g'g$.  The two cross

\begin{proposition}[the cross commutator]\label{prop:EF}
In $D$,
\[
F_sE_r-E_rF_s=\del_{rs}\,\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{(+)}-\cK_s^{(-)-1}\bigr) .
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Compute $E_rF_s$ — that is, the cross product $yx$ of \eqref{SK}
with $x=F_s\in\Uq(\bm)$, $y=E_r\in\Uq(\bp)$ — as channels over
\eqref{DE}: the $x$-channels (from $\Delta^2(F_s)$) are
$(F_s,\cK_s^{-1},\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1}),\ (1,1,F_s)$
and the $y$-channels (from $\Delta^2(E_r)$) are
$(E_r,1,1),\ (\cK_r,E_r,1),\ (\cK_r,\cK_r,E_r)$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) a channel survives only if no grouplike
pairs against a charged word, and $\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_s)=0$ kills
every $1$-versus-letter scalar.  The three survivors:
\begin{itemize}
\item $((F_s,\cK_s^{-1},\cK_s^{-1}),(E_r,1,1))$: first scalar
  $\la F_s,E_r\ra=\del_{rs}\tht$; middle slots
  $x_2=\cK_s^{-1}$, $y_2=1$ give the grouplike
  $\cK_s^{(-)-1}$; third scalar $\la\cK_s^{-1},1\ra=1$.
  Contribution: $\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_s^{(-)-1}$.
\item $((1,F_s,\cK_s^{-1}),(\cK_r,E_r,1))$: first scalar
  $\la1,\cK_r\ra=1$; middle slots $x_2=F_s$, $y_2=E_r$ give the
  pure tensor $F_s\otimes E_r$, the juxtaposed cross product
  written $F_sE_r$;
  third scalar $\la\cK_s^{-1},1\ra=1$.
  Contribution: the juxtaposition $F_sE_r$.
\item $((1,1,F_s),(\cK_r,\cK_r,E_r))$: first scalar
  $\la1,\cK_r\ra=1$; middle slots $1,\cK_r$ give the grouplike
  $\cK_r^{(+)}$; third scalar (using \eqref{S} and
  Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(d), second entry, with $v=-\alpha_r$)
  \[
  \la F_s,S^{-1}(E_r)\ra
  =-\la F_s,E_r\cK_r^{-1}\ra=-\del_{rs}\tht .
  \]
  Contribution: $-\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_r^{(+)}$.
\end{itemize}
Channels not listed contain a grouplike against a charged word, a
letter against a grouplike (both killed by \eqref{P} or
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b)), or a vanishing $\vep$-scalar.  Summing the
three contributions,
\[
E_rF_s=F_sE_r+\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_s^{(-)-1}
-\del_{rs}\tht\,\cK_r^{(+)},
\]
which rearranges to the stated identity.
(The same three channels, evaluated by the exact implementation of
\eqref{DE}, \eqref{PA}, \eqref{S}, give identical coefficients;
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.)
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[PBW basis of $D$]\label{rem:pbwD}
The cross rules (Lemma~\ref{lem:cross},
Proposition~\ref{prop:EF}) reduce the number of inversions relative to
the order $(\text{m-Cartans},F\text{'s})\times
(\text{p-Cartans},E\text{'s})$, so the ordered monomials
$\hK^{(-)\lambda}F^{\mathbf a}\,\hK^{(+)\mu}E^{\mathbf b}$ span $D$;
by the existence theorem (triangular decomposition of $D$) they are a
basis, the \emph{PBW basis} of $D$.
\end{remark}

\section{Part 1: the isomorphism}\label{sec:p1}

\begin{definition}\label{def:A}
$\Sn(\B^*)$ is the $\C$-algebra with generators $b_{ij},c_{ij}$
($1\le i,j\le n$; entries with $|i-j|\ge2$ are adjoined via the
quantum-minor recursions below) and relations:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item\label{relAA} inside the $b$'s, and inside the $c$'s, the
  relations of the quantum matrix algebra: the $b_{ij}$ form one
  copy $\mathsf T_q(n)$ of the upper-triangular quotient of the
  quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_q(M_n)$ and the $c_{ij}$ a
  second copy.
  In the horizontal-arc basis the fundamental generators are the
  diagonal and adjacent arcs; the relations then read as follows.
  The adjacent-pair exchanges are
  \[
  b_{i,i+1}b_{ii}=q\,b_{ii}b_{i,i+1},\qquad
  b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+1}=q^{-1}\,b_{i+1,i+1}b_{i,i+1},
  \]
  \[
  c_{i+1,i}c_{ii}=q\,c_{ii}c_{i+1,i},\qquad
  c_{i+1,i}c_{i+1,i+1}=q^{-1}\,c_{i+1,i+1}c_{i+1,i},
  \]
  disjoint pairs (non-interlacing endpoint intervals) commute, and
  the entries with $|i-j|\ge2$ are adjoined through the quantum
  minors
  \begin{equation}
  b_{i,i+2}\coloneqq b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+2}-q^{-1}b_{i+1,i+2}b_{i,i+1},
  \qquad
  c_{i+2,i}\coloneqq c_{i+2,i+1}c_{i+1,i}-q^{-1}c_{i+1,i}c_{i+2,i+1},
  \label{qmin}\tag{q-min}
  \end{equation}
  and recursively by the same formula for larger gaps.  The
  relations among entries at gaps $\ge2$ are those induced by these
  recursions from the displayed relations and the recursions
  themselves (the bigon-stacking telescoping), and the displayed
  adjacent exchanges realize the quantum matrix algebra
  $\mathcal O_q(M_n)$'s triangular copy $\mathsf T_q(n)$;
\item\label{relB} the mixed relations, for all admissible indices,
  \begin{align}
  c_{jj}\,b_{ii}&=b_{ii}\,c_{jj},
  \qquad
  c_{j+1,j}\,b_{ii}=q^{\alpha_j(i)}\,b_{ii}\,c_{j+1,j},
  \label{M0}\tag{M0}\\
  c_{jj}\,b_{i,i+1}&=
  \begin{cases}
  q\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j=i,\\
  q^{-1}\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j=i+1,\\
  b_{i,i+1}\,c_{jj} & j\notin\{i,i+1\},
  \end{cases}
  \label{M1}\tag{M1}\\
  c_{i+1,i}\,b_{i,i+1}&=b_{i,i+1}\,c_{i+1,i}
  +\tht\bigl(b_{ii}\,c_{i+1,i+1}-b_{i+1,i+1}\,c_{ii}\bigr),
  \label{M2}\tag{M2}\\
  c_{j+1,j}\,b_{i,i+1}&=
  \begin{cases}
  q\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{j+1,j} & j=i-1,\\
  q^{-1}\,b_{i,i+1}\,c_{j+1,j} & j=i+1,\\
  b_{i,i+1}\,c_{j+1,j} & j\notin\{i-1,i,i+1\},
  \end{cases}
  \qquad i.e.,\ \text{scalar}\ q^{\,\alpha_j(i+1)-\alpha_i(j+1)}
  \ (j\ne i),
  \label{M3}\tag{M3}
  \end{align}
\end{enumerate}
These are the relations of the bigon surface algebra in the
horizontal-arc basis: \eqref{relAA} is the arc algebra of each
boundary copy, and \eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} are the exchange relations
of the single essential mixed crossing configuration of the bigon:
crossing an upper arc $b$ against a lower arc $c$ is the
$\mathcal R$-matrix exchange, which produces a scalar
$q^{(\text{weight},\,\text{weight})}$ when the two arcs share exactly
one boundary mark — the $q^{\pm1}$ cases of \eqref{M0}, \eqref{M1},
\eqref{M3} — and which in the unique configuration \eqref{M2} where
the two arcs share both marks additionally produces the two-term
$\tht$-correction of the enclosed bigon face (the two smoothings of
the interior crossing; cf.\ the bigon case of L\^e's triangular
decomposition of stated skein algebras, with the boundary matching
fixing the displayed orientation of the $q^{\pm1}$ factors).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}\label{def:phi}
In $D$ set
\[
t_{ii}=\hK_i^{(+)},\qquad
t_{i,i+1}=E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)},\qquad
s_{ii}=\bigl(\hK_i^{(-)}\bigr)^{-1},\qquad
s_{i+1,i}=\bigl(\hK_{i+1}^{(-)}\bigr)^{-1}F_i
\]
(and their quantum minors for $|i-j|\ge2$), and define
$\Phi:\Sn(\B^*)\to D$ by $b_{ij}\mapsto t_{ij}$,
$c_{ij}\mapsto s_{ij}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[the \eqref{relAA}-relations]\label{prop:t}
The $t_{ij}$ and the $s_{ij}$ satisfy \eqref{relAA}: the adjacent
exchanges, the disjoint commutations, and the minor recursions
\eqref{qmin} all hold with $b\mapsto t$, $c\mapsto s$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Throughout, $\hK^{(\pm)}$-grouplikes commute among themselves, and
within each Borel \eqref{H1} in the form
\begin{equation}
\hK_i^{(\pm)}E_r\hK_i^{(\pm)-1}=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r,\qquad
\hK_i^{(\pm)}F_r\hK_i^{(\pm)-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_r
\label{H1pm}\tag{H1$^\pm$}
\end{equation}
moves a letter past a grouplike at the cost of a $q^{\pm1}$-scalar;
by \eqref{A2}, $\alpha_i(i)=-1$ and $\alpha_i(i+1)=+1$.

\emph{First adjacent pair.}  Moving $\hK_i^{(+)}$ past $E_i$ by

\begin{theorem}[the mixed relations hold in $D$]\label{thm:mixed}
With $t,s$ as in Definition~\ref{def:phi}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item (M0) $s_{jj}t_{ii}=t_{ii}s_{jj}$;
\item (M1) $s_{j+1,j}t_{ii}=q^{\alpha_j(i)}t_{ii}s_{j+1,j}$;
\item (M1$'$) $s_{jj}t_{i,i+1}=q^{-\alpha_i(j)}\,t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$,
  i.e.\ equals $q\,t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$ for $j=i$, equals
  $q^{-1}t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$ for $j=i+1$, and equals $t_{i,i+1}s_{jj}$
  for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$;
\item (M3)
  $s_{j+1,j}t_{i,i+1}=q^{\alpha_j(i+1)-\alpha_i(j+1)}\,
  t_{i,i+1}s_{j+1,j}$ for $j\ne i$; the exponent is $+1$ for
  $j=i-1$, $-1$ for $j=i+1$, $0$ otherwise;
\item (M2) $s_{i+1,i}t_{i,i+1}
  =t_{i,i+1}s_{i+1,i}
  +\tht\bigl(t_{ii}s_{i+1,i+1}-t_{i+1,i+1}s_{ii}\bigr)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
(a): Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c).

(b): by Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(b) (with exponent
$\alpha_j(i)$) followed by Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c) for the initial
commuting m-grouplike:
\[
s_{j+1,j}t_{ii}
=\hK_{j+1}^{(-)-1}F_j\hK_i^{(+)}
=\hK_{j+1}^{(-)-1}\bigl(q^{\alpha_j(i)}\hK_i^{(+)}F_j\bigr)
=q^{\alpha_j(i)}\,\hK_i^{(+)}s_{j+1,j}.
\]

(c): compute in grouplike-to-the-rear order by \eqref{aInv} for the
m-grouplike crossing and Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c) to order the two
grouplikes:
\[
s_{jj}t_{i,i+1}
=\hK_j^{(-)-1}E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
=q^{-\alpha_i(j)}\,E_i\hK_j^{(-)-1}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
=q^{-\alpha_i(j)}\,E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}\hK_j^{(-)-1}
=q^{-\alpha_i(j)}\,t_{i,i+1}s_{jj},
\]
and by \eqref{A2} the exponent $-\alpha_i(j)$ is $+1$ for $j=i$,
$-1$ for $j=i+1$, and $0$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, as claimed in
\eqref{M1}.

(d): for $j\ne i$, Proposition~\ref{prop:EF} gives
$F_jE_i=E_iF_j$.  Hence
\[
s_{j+1,j}t_{i,i+1}
=\hK_{j+1}^{(-)-1}F_jE_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
=\hK_{j+1}^{(-)-1}E_iF_j\hK_{i+1}^{(+)} .
\]
Move the letters to the front: by the grouplike-weight version of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a) applied at $u=-e_{j+1}$ (the pairing value
$\la g^{-1},\cK_i\ra=\la g,\cK_i\ra^{-1}$ inverts the scalar of the
unique channel), and by Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(b),
\[

\[
\alpha_i(j+1)=\del_{j+1,i+1}-\del_{j+1,i},
\qquad
\alpha_j(i+1)=\del_{i+1,j+1}-\del_{i+1,j},
\]
so for $j\neq i$ the exponent $\alpha_j(i+1)-\alpha_i(j+1)$ equals
$0+1=+1$ at $j=i-1$, $-1-0=-1$ at $j=i+1$, and $0$ otherwise,
i.e.\ $\del_{j,i-1}-\del_{j,i+1}$.  Ordering the two grouplikes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c) (no scalar),
\[
s_{j+1,j}t_{i,i+1}
=q^{\,\del_{j,i-1}-\del_{j,i+1}}\,
E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}\hK_{j+1}^{(-)-1}F_j
=q^{\,\del_{j,i-1}-\del_{j,i+1}}\,t_{i,i+1}s_{j+1,j},

\[

\[

\[

\begin{theorem}[Part 1]\label{thm:one}
$\Phi:\Sn(\B^*)\to D$ is a well-defined algebra isomorphism.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\emph{Well-defined.}  \eqref{relAA} by Proposition~\ref{prop:t};
\eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} by Theorem~\ref{thm:mixed}(a)--(e), using
$t_{ii}s_{j+1,j+1}=\Phi(b_{ii}c_{j+1,j+1})$ etc.; the gap-$\ge2$
relations descend by the shared minor recursions on both sides.

\emph{PBW bijection.}  \eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} order every mixed
word: \eqref{M0}, \eqref{M1}, \eqref{M3} exchange a mixed pair at
the cost of a nonzero scalar, and \eqref{M2} exchanges the unique
remaining pair at the cost of diagonal-only extra terms; the
$\mathcal O_q(M_n)$-PBW theorem then reduces each copy to ordered
monomials, so ordered monomials span $\Sn(\B^*)$.  Under $\Phi$
they map to the ordered monomials of $D$
(Remark~\ref{rem:pbwD}), with the exponent data of each factor
preserved; since the latter form a basis of $D$, the spanning set
is independent and $\Phi$ is a bijection.

\emph{Consequences.}  The loop
$\omega_i=b_{ii}c_{ii}$ is invertible in $\Sn(\B^*)$ (its image
$\Omega_i$ is a product of units); as $b_{ii},c_{ii}$ commute by
\eqref{M0}, both are invertible with
$b_{ii}^{-1}=\omega_i^{-1}c_{ii}$.  Explicitly,
$\hK_i^{(+)}=\Phi(b_{ii})$,
$E_i=\Phi\bigl(b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+1}^{-1}\bigr)$,
$\hK_i^{(-)}=\Phi\bigl(c_{ii}^{-1}\bigr)$,
$F_i=\Phi\bigl(c_{i+1,i+1}^{-1}c_{i+1,i}\bigr)$.
\end{proof}

'"\\begin{equation}

'"\\item\\label{Tc} For grouplike weights "'$u$,
  '"\\[
  \\la\\hK"'^{u}F_s,E_r'"\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht\\,q"'^{+'"\\alpha_s(u)},\\qquad
  \\la F_s\\hK"'^{u},E_r'"\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht .
  \\]
  In particular, with "'$'"\\cK_s"'^{'"\\pm1}=\\hK"'^{'"\\mp\\alpha_s}"'$,
  '"\\[
  \\la\\cK_s"'^{'"\\pm1}F_s,E_r\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht\\,q"'^{'"\\mp2}\\qquad
  (\\text{since }\\alpha_s\\cdot\\alpha_s=-2).
  \\]
\\item\\label{Td} For grouplike weights "'$v$,
  '"\\[
  \\la F_s,\\hK"'^{v}E_r'"\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht\\,q"'^{-'"\\alpha_s(v)},\\qquad
  \\la F_s,E_r\\hK"'^{v}'"\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht .
  \\]
  In particular,
  \\[
  \\la F_s,\\cK_r"'^{'"\\pm1}E_r\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht\\,q"'^{'"\\mp2},\\qquad
  \\la F_s,\\hK_rE_r\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\,\\tht\\,q"'^{+1},'"\\qquad
  \\la F_r,\\hK_{r+1}E_r\\ra=\\tht\\,q"'^{-1}.
  '"\\]
\\end{enumerate}
\\end{lemma}
\\begin{proof}
Note first that for "'$w'"\\in\\Z"'^n$ and any root vector $'"\\alpha_r"'$,
'"\\begin{equation}
w\\cdot\\alpha_r=-\\alpha_r(w),\\qquad
\\alpha_r\\cdot w=-\\alpha_r(w),
\\tag{"'$'"\\ast"'$}
'"\\end{equation}
because "'$'"\\sum_i\\alpha_r(i)=0"'$ kills the $'"\\tfrac1n"'$-part of
$a_{ij}$, and $'"\\alpha_r\\cdot e_i=\\alpha_r(i)"'$.
(a): bimultiplicativity from '"\\eqref{PA} with grouplike coproducts and
\\eqref{P}, then \\eqref{A2}.
(b): in every \\eqref{PA}-channel one factor pairs a grouplike against
a word containing a root letter, which vanishes by \\eqref{P}; the
grouplike-vs-grouplike bimultiplicativity also gives
"'$'"\\la\\hK"'^u,yz'"\\ra=\\la\\hK"'^u,z'"\\ra\\la\\hK"'^u,y'"\\ra"'$ directly, so the claim
holds for grouplikes on either side in either position.
(c): by '"\\eqref{P} and (b), the only channel of
"'$'"\\Delta(F_s)=F_s\\otimes\\cK_s"'^{-1}+1'"\\otimes F_s"'$ against $E_r$
contributing to the first line of '"\\eqref{PA} is
"'$'"\\la\\hK"'^uF_s,E_r'"\\ra
=\\la F_s,E_r\\ra\\la\\hK"'^u,'"\\cK_r\\ra
=\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{'"\\,u\\cdot\\alpha_r}
\\overset{(\\ast)}{=}\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{+'"\\alpha_s(u)}"'$ for $r=s$;
for the second, splitting off $'"\\hK"'^u$ with the second line of
'"\\eqref{PA} against "'$'"\\Delta(E_r)=E_r\\otimes1+\\cK_r\\otimes E_r"'$ leaves
the $'"\\vep"'$-free channel
$'"\\la F_s\\hK"'^u,E_r'"\\ra
=\\la F_s,E_r\\ra\\la\\hK"'^u,1'"\\ra
+\\la F_s,\\cK_r\\ra\\la\\hK"'^u,E_r'"\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\tht"'$.
(d): the $S$-twisted charged-letter minor of '"\\eqref{PA} (split the
rightmost letter of the second argument against the \\emph{second}
coproduct factor of "'$F_s$):
'"\\[
\\la F_s,\\hK"'^{v}E_r'"\\ra
=\\la\\cK_s"'^{-1},'"\\hK"'^v'"\\ra\\la F_s,E_r\\ra
=\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{(-'"\\alpha_s)\\cdot v}
\\overset{(\\ast)}{=}\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{-'"\\alpha_s(v)},\\qquad
\\la F_s,E_r\\hK"'^{v}'"\\ra
=\\la\\cK_s"'^{-1},E_r'"\\ra\\la F_s,\\hK"'^v'"\\ra
+\\la F_s,E_r\\ra\\la1,\\hK"'^v'"\\ra
=\\del_{rs}\\tht,
\\]
where the vanishing terms die by \\eqref{P}, (b), and
"'$'"\\vep(E_r)=0"'$, and $'"\\la\\cK_s"'^{-1},'"\\hK"'^v'"\\ra=q"'^{-'"\\alpha_s\\cdot v}"'$ by
(a).  The '"\\emph{in particular} values use "'$'"\\alpha_s\\cdot\\alpha_s=-2"'$
and $'"\\alpha_r(s)=-\\del_{rs}"'$, $'"\\alpha_r(r+1)=+1"'$ from '"\\eqref{A2}.
(All values were obtained by the exact recursive implementation of
\\eqref{PA}, \\eqref{P}, \\eqref{C} in this "'$S$-twisted slot order;
Remark~'"\\ref{rem:verify}: the four placement families at all
"'$(r,s,i)$ and at random weights, $n=2,3,4$.)
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{remark}\\label{rem:compatSK}
The form is well-defined on "'$'"\\Uq(\\bm)\\times\\Uq(\\bp)"'$: for the
external existence theorem this is part of Definition~'"\\ref{def:D},
and the elementary content is Lemma~\\ref{lem:compat}.
\\end{remark}

\\begin{lemma}[compatibility checks]\\label{lem:compat}
The recursion \\eqref{PA}, \\eqref{P} is consistent with the Borel
relations \\eqref{H1}, \\eqref{H3} on both sides:
\\begin{enumerate}[label=(\\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\\item\\label{Cist} "'$'"\\la\\hK_iF_s\\hK_i"'^{-1},E_r'"\\ra
 =q"'^{'"\\,+\\alpha_r(i)}\\la F_s,E_r\\ra"'$ for all $i,r,s$;
'"\\item\\label{Cist2} "'$'"\\la F_s,\\hK_iE_r\\hK_i"'^{-1}'"\\ra
 =q"'^{'"\\,-\\alpha_r(i)}\\la F_s,E_r\\ra"'$ for all $i,r,s$;
'"\\item\\label{Ci} every relator of \\eqref{H3} (and its "'$F$-analogue)
 pairs to zero against grouplikes and against all words of root
 charge $'"\\pm1"'$; against grouplikes, every charged tensor of
 '"\\eqref{H1}, \\eqref{H3} also pairs to zero.
\\end{enumerate}
\\end{lemma}
\\begin{proof}
\\eqref{Cist}: apply the second line of \\eqref{PA} with
"'$'"\\Delta(E_r)=E_r\\otimes1+\\cK_r\\otimes E_r"'$ three times — the first
argument $'"\\hK_iF_s\\hK_i"'^{-1}$ is split letter by letter, and each
slot of $'"\\Delta"'^2(E_r)
=E_r'"\\otimes1\\otimes1+\\cK_r\\otimes E_r\\otimes1
+\\cK_r\\otimes\\cK_r\\otimes E_r"'$ is met by one letter:
'"\\[
\\la\\hK_iF_s\\hK_i"'^{-1},E_r'"\\ra
=\\underbrace{\\la\\hK_i,E_r\\ra[\\,1\\,]\\la F_s,1\\ra}_{=\\,0\\
\\text{by Lemma~\\ref{lem:T}(b)}}\\,
+\\,\\la\\hK_i,\\cK_r\\ra\\la F_s,E_r\\ra\\la\\hK_i"'^{-1},1'"\\ra
=q"'^{'"\\,e_i\\cdot\\alpha_r}\\,\\del_{rs}\\tht
=\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{-'"\\alpha_r(i)},
\\]
using "'$e_i'"\\cdot\\alpha_r=-\\alpha_r(i)"'$ from $('"\\ast)"'$.
Since '"\\eqref{H1} gives
"'$'"\\hK_iF_s\\hK_i"'^{-1}=q''^{-'"\\alpha_s(i)}F_s"'$, the relation replaces the
left argument by $q''^{-'"\\alpha_s(i)}F_s"'$; and
$'"\\la F_s,E_r\\ra=\\del_{rs}\\tht"'$ is nonzero only for $r=s$, where the
two scalars agree: consistency holds.
'"\\eqref{Cist2}: the "'$S$-twisted minor '"\\eqref{PA} against the word
"'$'"\\hK"'^{v_1}E_r'"\\hK"'^{v_2}$ (split off the rightmost grouplike against
the second coproduct factor of $F_s$, then the $E_r$-letter) gives
the placement formula
'"\\begin{equation}
\\la F_s,\\,\\hK"'^{v_1}E_r'"\\hK"'^{v_2}'"\\ra
=\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{'"\\,(-\\alpha_s)\\cdot v_1}
\\qquad(v_1,v_2\\in\\Z"'^n):'"\\label{auxE}\\tag{"'$'"\\dagger"'$}
'"\\end{equation}
splitting "'$'"\\hK"'^{v_2}$ off first, the channel through
$'"\\la\\cK_s"'^{-1},'"\\cdot\\ra"'$ against the $E_r$-letter vanishes by
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:T}(b) and the surviving channel is
"'$'"\\la F_s,\\hK"'^{v_1}E_r'"\\ra\\la1,\\hK"'^{v_2}'"\\ra"'$; the former is
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:T}(d).  Taking "'$v_1=e_i$, $v_2=-e_i$ and using
$(-'"\\alpha_s)\\cdot e_i=+\\alpha_s(i)"'$ from '"\\eqref{A2},
\\[
\\la F_s,\\hK_iE_r\\hK_i"'^{-1}'"\\ra
=\\del_{rs}\\tht\\,q"'^{+'"\\alpha_s(i)} .
\\]
For "'$r'"\\neq s"'$ both sides vanish, and for $r=s$ '"\\eqref{H1} replaces
the word by "'$q''^{+'"\\alpha_r(i)}E_r"'$; consistency holds exactly on the
support of $'"\\la F_s,E_r\\ra"'$.  (The channel enumeration of
'"\\eqref{auxE} at all "'$(i,r,s)$, $n=2,3$, and at general weights was
performed in the exact model; Remark~'"\\ref{rem:verify}.)
\\eqref{Ci}: against grouplikes, any relator of \\eqref{H1},
\\eqref{H3} is a tensor of nonzero root charge or a difference of two
terms of distinct weight; in each \\eqref{PA}-channel one factor
pairs a grouplike against a charged word and vanishes by
Lemma~\\ref{lem:T}(b).  Against words of root charge "'$'"\\pm1"'$: the
'"\\eqref{H3}-tensors have root charge "'$'"\\pm2,\\pm3"'$, so every channel
has a grouplike-against-charged or unequal-charge factor and
vanishes by '"\\eqref{P}, Lemma~\\ref{lem:T}(b) (pairings are
charge-graded: "'$'"\\la u,y\\ra\\neq0"'$ requires equal total root charge,
immediate from '"\\eqref{PA}, \\eqref{P} by induction on word length).
\\end{proof}

$(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(g,g,g)$ and $S(y_1)=g^{-1}$:

We compare the three summands with the right-hand side of (M2).

\emph{First summand.}
\[
W\coloneqq\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}E_iF_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
\overset{\text{(a)}}{=}q^{-1}\,E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}F_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}
\overset{\text{(b)}}{=}q^{-1}q^{+1}\,
 E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}F_i ,
\]
where the first crossing is Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a) with the
inverse grouplike: from
$E_r\hK^{u(-)}=q^{\,u\cdot\alpha_r}\hK^{u(-)}E_r$ at $u=-e_{i+1}$,
$E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}=q^{\alpha_i(i+1)}\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}E_i
=q^{+1}\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}E_i$, i.e.\
$\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}E_i=q^{-1}E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}$; and the second is
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(b),
$F_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}=q^{\alpha_i(i+1)}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}F_i
=q^{+1}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}F_i$.  The two scalars cancel, the grouplikes
commute by Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c), and
\[
W=E_i\hK_{i+1}^{(+)}\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}F_i=t_{i,i+1}s_{i+1,i}.
\]

\emph{Second summand.}
\[
\tht\,\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}\cK_i^{(+)}\hK_{i+1}^{(+)} ;

by Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c) the initial $\hK_{i+1}^{(-)-1}$ commutes

\emph{PBW bijection.}  \eqref{M0}--\eqref{M3} order every mixed
word: \eqref{M0}, \eqref{M1}, \eqref{M3} exchange a mixed pair at
the cost of a nonzero scalar, and \eqref{M2} exchanges the unique
remaining pair at the cost of diagonal-only extra terms; the
$\mathcal O_q(M_n)$-PBW theorem then reduces each copy to ordered
monomials, so ordered monomials span $\Sn(\B^*)$.  Under $\Phi$
they map to the ordered monomials of $D$
(Remark~\ref{rem:pbwD}), with the exponent data of each factor
preserved; since the latter form a basis of $D$, the spanning set
is independent and $\Phi$ is a bijection.

\emph{Consequences.}  The loop
$\omega_i=b_{ii}c_{ii}$ is invertible in $\Sn(\B^*)$ (its image
$\Omega_i$ is a product of units); as $b_{ii},c_{ii}$ commute by
\eqref{M0}, both are invertible with
$b_{ii}^{-1}=\omega_i^{-1}c_{ii}$.  Explicitly,
$\hK_i^{(+)}=\Phi(b_{ii})$,
$E_i=\Phi\bigl(b_{i,i+1}b_{i+1,i+1}^{-1}\bigr)$,
$\hK_i^{(-)}=\Phi\bigl(c_{ii}^{-1}\bigr)$,
$F_i=\Phi\bigl(c_{i+1,i+1}^{-1}c_{i+1,i}\bigr)$.
\end{proof}

\section{Quantum-group data and the double}\label{sec:qg}

\subsection{The simply-connected quantum group}

Set
\[
a_{ij}=\tfrac1n-\del_{ij}\ (1\le i,j\le n),\qquad
\alpha_r(i)=\del_{i,r+1}-\del_{i,r}\ (1\le r\le n-1),\qquad
\tht=(q^{-1}-q)^{-1}.
\]
Then $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and
\begin{equation}
\alpha_r(r)=-1,\quad \alpha_r(r+1)=+1,\quad \alpha_r(i)=0\
(i\notin\{r,r+1\}),\qquad \alpha_r\cdot\alpha_s=-2\del_{rs},
\label{A2}\tag{A2}
\end{equation}
where $u\cdot v=\sum_{i,j}u_iv_ja_{ij}$ (symmetric) for
$u,v\in\Z^n$, and we identify $\alpha_r$ with its coordinate vector
(the $\tfrac1n$-part of $a_{ij}$ drops out of $\alpha_r\cdot v$
because $\sum_i\alpha_r(i)=0$, so
$\alpha_r\cdot e_i=\alpha_r(i)$ for the standard basis $e_i$).

\begin{definition}\label{def:H}
$H=\Uq^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$ is the $\C$-algebra generated by
abelian grouplikes $\hK_i^{\pm1}$ ($1\le i\le n$) and $E_r,F_r$
($1\le r\le n-1$) subject to
\begin{align}
\hK_iE_r\hK_i^{-1}&=q^{\alpha_r(i)}E_r,\qquad
\hK_iF_r\hK_i^{-1}=q^{-\alpha_r(i)}F_r,\label{H1}\tag{H1}\\
E_rF_s-F_sE_r&=\del_{rs}\,\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r\bigr)
\qquad(\cK_r\coloneqq\hK_r\hK_{r+1}^{-1}),\label{H2}\tag{H2}
\end{align}
and the quantum Serre relations
\begin{equation}
E_r^2E_s-(q+q^{-1})E_rE_sE_r+E_sE_r^2=0\ \ (|r-s|=1),\qquad
E_rE_s=E_sE_r\ \ (|r-s|>1),\label{H3}\tag{H3}
\end{equation}
with their $F$-analogues.  Its Hopf algebra structure — and that of
each Borel subalgebra separately — is fixed by
\begin{equation}
\Delta\hK_i=\hK_i\otimes\hK_i,\qquad
\Delta E_r=E_r\otimes1+\cK_r\otimes E_r,\qquad
\Delta F_r=F_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}+1\otimes F_r,\label{C}\tag{C}
\end{equation}
$\vep(\hK_i)=1$, $\vep(E_r)=\vep(F_r)=0$, hence
\begin{equation}
S\hK_i=\hK_i^{-1},\qquad SE_r=-\cK_r^{-1}E_r,\qquad
S^{-1}E_r=-E_r\cK_r^{-1},\label{S}\tag{S}
\end{equation}
and $SF_r=-F_r\cK_r=-q^{-2}\cK_rF_r$,
$S^{-1}F_r=-\cK_rF_r=-q^{2}F_r\cK_r^{-1}$ (using
$\cK_rF_r=q^{2}F_r\cK_r$ from \eqref{H1}, which likewise gives
$\cK_rE_r=q^{-2}E_r\cK_r$).  Only the three values displayed in
\eqref{S} enter the channel calculus below.
The Borel subalgebras are the subalgebras
$\Uq(\bp)=\la\hK_i,E_r\ra$ and $\Uq(\bm)=\la\hK_i,F_r\ra$ with the
restricted Hopf algebra structures.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[consistency of the coproduct]\label{rem:hopfok}
$\Delta$ descends to the quotient by \eqref{H1}--\eqref{H3}: on
\eqref{H1} both sides of the relator are grouplike times the letter,
and \eqref{C} respects the exponent; on \eqref{H3} it is the standard
quantum-Serre computation; and on \eqref{H2} the mixed products
expand as
\[
\Delta(E_r)\Delta(F_r)-\Delta(F_r)\Delta(E_r)
=\tht\bigl(\cK_r^{-1}\otimes\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r\otimes\cK_r\bigr)
=\Delta\bigl(\tht(\cK_r^{-1}-\cK_r)\bigr),
\]
since the two $E_r\otimes F_r$-terms cancel and the remaining cross
terms $\cK_rF_r\otimes E_r\cK_r^{-1}-F_r\cK_r\otimes\cK_r^{-1}E_r$
vanish: by \eqref{H1} the tensorands agree pairwise with equal
scalars ($\cK_rF_r=q^{2}F_r\cK_r$ and
$E_r\cK_r^{-1}=q^{-2}\cK_r^{-1}E_r$).  These are exactly the defining
Hopf-algebra checks of $U_q^{ext}(\mathfrak{sl}(n))$;
Remark~\ref{rem:verify}.  Counit and antipode descend as well.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[why these conventions]\label{rem:whyC}
The problem's normalization \eqref{P0} has
$\la E_i,F_j\ra=\tht\,\del_{ij}$, while Tanisaki's $\tau$ is often
normalized with the opposite sign; the form of \eqref{C} above is
chosen so that the cross commutator induced on the diagonal quotient
recovers \eqref{H2} in precisely the printed sign
(Proposition~\ref{prop:EF} and Lemma~\ref{lem:diag}).  Any of the
neighbouring conventions — replacing $S^{-1}$ by $S$ in \eqref{SK},
or flipping the coproduct Cartan of one Borel — is detected as an
incompatibility in the channel calculus: the \eqref{H1}-compatibility
of Lemma~\ref{lem:compat} fails, or the diagonal commutator acquires
the opposite sign.  The present choices are pinned by these
requirements, and each was re-derived, not borrowed, from
\eqref{PA}--\eqref{P}.
\end{remark}
